correctness.rationale: For an existing balanced thick generalized hexagon, the intersection array gives distance polynomials and seven adjacency sectors ±(q+1), 0, ±sqrt(q), ±sqrt(3q). Its point/line sign sector is exactly the stated Fq(p); other centered sectors are below it for 0<p<1. I independently reconstructed the critical exact Bernstein certificate: three bidegree-(8,5) tensor arrays of 54 strictly positive rational coefficients each, minima 885/2048, 1677/10240 and 381/40960, so the nontrivial small-z comparison holds uniformly q≥2; large-z comparison uses the factorized generating polynomials and elementary sign inequalities. The fractional-power integral transfers generating-function comparison to spectral ordering. Summation-by-parts proves Fq strictly increasing from −1 at p=0 to >0 at p=1, giving the unique threshold. The sector nullity one at the endpoint and Schoenberg Gram rank v−2 follow. Fq(0)=−1 and Fq’(0)=q⁵log(6/5)+O(q⁴), bounded Fq’’ yield αq=1/[q⁵log(6/5)]+O(q^-6). Independent q=2,3,4,7,10,30 sector evaluations corroborated but are not the infinite-order proof.
